absent_flag_policy: The Python driver holds only on an explicit false, so this candidate is additive: with the older installed bridge nothing changes, and with it installed the refusal class is prevented rather than retried.

binary_verification.lineage: installed hash equals the authorised sts2mcp-victory-flag candidate, and the candidate still carries is_victory, so the delta is two added fields rather than a different lineage
binary_verification.method: searched the compiled assembly heaps in both UTF-8 and UTF-16LE; a presence check on metadata, not a claim about runtime behaviour
binary_verification.usage_string_verdict: NOT provable this way: the substring 'usage' already occurs in the installed assembly, so its presence says nothing about the new field.  The published key is verified by a live health/state smoke after an install, and nothing before that should claim it works.

build.command: powershell -File third_party/STS2MCP-main/build.ps1 -GameDir "G:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Slay the Spire 2"  (with the repo's vendored SDK on PATH)

driver_side_hooks.discard_then_buy: advisor_core/live_choice_policy.potion_to_discard_for + policy_live._shop, works on the installed bridge

install_requires: explicit operator authorisation for this purpose, a game+port idle window, and scripts/stage_sts2mcp.py --apply; the previous authorisations were granted for the victory flag and for the decline-without-buying probe and are not treated as a general licence
purpose: Publish the two preconditions an automated player cannot infer: whether a rest site can take a choice yet, and what each held potion's usage actually is.

source_delta.change: rest_site gains can_choose = (NRestSiteRoom.Instance is not null); each entry in player.potions gains usage = potion.Usage.ToString(). No route, action or other field touched; can_use_in_combat kept as-is so existing readers are unaffected.

why_needed.authority: The refusal is the mod's own guard, so the guard is what gets published -- the same shape as can_proceed on the same screen and is_victory on game_over.
why_needed.not_solved_by_a_driver_rule: Waiting a fixed number of polls was measured and rejected: the refused frame at seq 4126 and the accepted frame at seq 4133 in ssb-20260921T124324Z-045dcccc are byte-identical in the fields the state exposes (same options, is_enabled true, can_proceed false).  No driver-side rule can separate them.
why_needed.potion_usage: can_use_in_combat is true for both CombatOnly and AnyTime, so the installed state cannot tell a potion that may be drunk between fights from one that may not. Measured on the real client: 鲜血药水 (heal) and 果汁 (+5 max HP) were held across 3,285 out-of-combat frames with no action available for them, and discard_potion/use_potion appear 0 times in the posted-action census of every recorded batch. AnyTime is 4 of the build's 64 potions.
why_needed.problem: BuildRestSiteState emits options from the RestSiteRoom *model* while ExecuteChooseRestOption (McpMod.Actions.cs:373-375) refuses while NRestSiteRoom.Instance is null.  Measured on this machine: 8 of 80 choose_rest_option posts recorded across the stored traces came back 'Rest site room is not open' (2 of 44 in the batches running today).  A full Act 1-3 run rests 5-7 times, so the full-run contract's 'every action was legal and acked' check is a coin flip on timing rather than a property of the player.
